newsitem.title: FRANCE: Italian lira sales annoy European partners-paper.
newsitem.headline: Italian lira sales annoy European partners-paper.

text.p: The French and other European governments have been irritated by Bank of Italy intervention to prevent the lira from strengthening too much, French daily Le Monde reported on Tuesday.

The paper said the displeasure in Paris and Bonn could delay a lira re-entry into the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), which Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has said would happen before the end of November.
Le Monde reported that for the past several weeks the Bank of Italy has been intervening "massively", through investment funds, to sell the lira whenever it reaches 1,005 per mark.

"We have bought significant quantities of the lira without making the level move," Le Monde quoted an unnamed U.S. fund manager saying. "There is little doubt that an invisible hand is intervening to sell the Italian currency."
Italy and France have been split on the right level for a lira re-entry to the ERM. "This attitude is not proper," Le Monde quoted a French official as saying.
Le Monde said French and German officials have set 950 lira per mark as a desired re-entry level.
It said the Italian government has been trying to prevent the lira rejoining at what it considers too strong a pivot level
Italian Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said on November 6 that 1,000 to 1,050 per mark is the likely range.
